positions.title: Software Engineer III
positions.locationName: San Jose, California, United States · Remote
positions.description: Performed white-box security assessments of Cohesity products, developed proof-of-concept exploits, and led remediation efforts with engineering teams. Reverse-engineered malware samples to identify targeting techniques and behaviors.

positions.title: Senior Security Engineer
positions.description: Performed white-box security assessments of Veritas products through source code audits and live system analysis. Developed proof-of-concept exploits, reported vulnerabilities with detailed analysis and CVSS scoring, and implemented code fixes in collaboration with the engineering teams.

positions.title: SQA Engineer / Technical Lead
positions.locationName: St Cloud, Minnesota, United States · On-site
positions.description: Developed automated tests for Symantec products within a proprietary Perl-based testing framework and conducted code reviews for quality and security. Mentoring team members on design and implementation best practices while serving as a technical lead.

educations.fieldOfStudy: Major: Applied Computer Science, Minor: Information Systems

honors.title: CypherCon 8 Internet Service Provider Capture the Flag (ISP CTF)
honors.description: Placed 1st (team of three) in the CypherCon 8 ISP CTF which involved web exploitation, network pivoting, privilege escalation, and exploiting system misconfigurations.

honors.title: DEF CON 32 "? Cube" Contest
honors.description: Placed 1st (team of five) in the DEF CON 32 "? Cube" Contest which involved cryptography, forensics, and web exploitation challenges.

projects.title: Trusted Platform Module (TPM) Research
projects.description: Designed and implemented new TPM 2.0 traffic capturing techniques and built a low-cost tool for extracting Volume Master Keys (VMKs) from discrete TPM chips.

projects.title: Linux on the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES)
projects.description: Demonstrated that the NES could run a UNIX-like operating system by porting one from the Commodore 64. Later developed an IBM PC emulator that runs on NES hardware, enabling a minimal Linux distribution to boot to a usable shell.
